questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: Cholera is characterised by:
options: Painless profuse rice-watery stools with rapid dehydration and no fever
questions.concept: Vibrio cholerae toxin irreversibly activates adenylate cyclase, causing massive secretory diarrhoea. Death is from hypovolaemic shock within hours, so rapid rehydration is life-saving.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: In a cholera outbreak, the single most important intervention is:
options: Prompt rehydration of cases with ORS and intravenous fluids
questions.concept: Rehydration reduces case fatality from over 30% to under 1%. Antibiotics shorten shedding but are secondary, and quarantine is ineffective and not recommended.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: Typhoid fever is confirmed most reliably in the first week by:
questions.concept: Blood culture is positive in about 80% in week one, bone marrow culture has the highest yield throughout, and stool and urine cultures become positive in weeks two and three.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: The chronic carrier state in typhoid is most often located in the:
options: Gallbladder, especially in women with gallstones
questions.concept: Chronic carriers excrete organisms for over a year and are a persisting source of infection, as illustrated by Typhoid Mary. Cholecystectomy may be needed when antibiotics fail.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: Hepatitis A and E differ from B and C in that they are:
options: Transmitted by the faeco-oral route and never become chronic
questions.concept: Hepatitis E is particularly severe in the third trimester of pregnancy with mortality up to 20%. Hepatitis B and C are blood-borne and cause chronic infection, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: The most infectious body fluid for hepatitis B transmission is:
options: Blood, with the risk after needlestick around 30 percent in the non-immune
questions.concept: Hepatitis B is far more transmissible than HIV, which carries about 0.3% risk. Vaccination of health workers, mandatory blood screening and safe injection practice are the pillars of prevention.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: Soil-transmitted helminth control in India is implemented through:
options: National Deworming Day with biannual albendazole for children and adolescents
questions.concept: Mass drug administration is combined with sanitation and hygiene promotion, since reinfection is rapid where open defecation persists - which is why deworming alone is insufficient.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: The infective form of hookworm entering through the skin is the:
questions.concept: Larvae penetrate the feet causing ground itch, migrate through lungs and mature in the duodenum where they suck blood, causing iron deficiency anaemia and hypoproteinaemia.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: The key epidemiological feature making cholera amenable to control is:
options: Transmission through contaminated water and food, interruptible by safe water and sanitation
questions.concept: John Snow's removal of the Broad Street pump handle in 1854 demonstrated waterborne transmission before the organism was known, founding modern epidemiology.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Diarrhoeal disease, enteric fever, hepatitis & helminths
questions.stem: Rotavirus vaccine was introduced into the Indian national schedule to reduce:
options: Severe dehydrating diarrhoea and diarrhoeal deaths in infants
questions.concept: Given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks with the pentavalent vaccine, it targets the leading cause of severe infantile gastroenteritis, complementing ORS and zinc in diarrhoea control.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The Bhore Committee of 1946 recommended:
options: Integration of preventive and curative services with a three-tier structure and primary health centres
questions.concept: Formally the Health Survey and Development Committee, it laid the foundation of India's public health system, including the principle that no one should be denied care for inability to pay.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The Mudaliar Committee of 1961 principally recommended:
options: Strengthening existing PHCs rather than opening new ones, and improving district hospitals
questions.concept: Formally the Health Survey and Planning Committee, it found existing PHCs inadequately staffed and equipped, arguing for consolidation before expansion.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The Kartar Singh Committee of 1973 is remembered for introducing:
options: The concept of the multipurpose health worker
questions.concept: It recommended replacing single-purpose workers with multipurpose male and female workers, each serving 5000 population, supervised by health assistants - the structure still in use.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The Srivastava Committee of 1975 recommended creation of:
options: Bands of paraprofessional and semi-professional health workers from the community
questions.concept: It led to the Community Health Volunteer scheme and ultimately influenced the ASHA concept, recognising that community-based workers are essential to extend coverage.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The National Health Policy 2017 set a target for public health expenditure of:
questions.concept: It also aims to raise life expectancy to 70, reduce under-five mortality to 23 by 2025 and reduce out-of-pocket expenditure, with an emphasis on comprehensive primary health care.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The National Rural Health Mission was launched in 2005 principally to:
options: Improve rural health infrastructure and outcomes with community participation and flexible financing
questions.concept: Key innovations were the ASHA, untied funds, Rogi Kalyan Samitis and village committees. It merged with the urban mission in 2013 to form the National Health Mission.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: Health planning in India is now guided by:
options: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission in 2015
questions.concept: Health is a state subject under the Constitution, with the centre providing policy direction and funding, making centre-state coordination essential for programme implementation.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The Chadah Committee dealt with:
options: Malaria maintenance phase, recommending surveillance by basic health workers
questions.concept: It proposed that malaria vigilance be integrated with general health services rather than run vertically - an early recognition of the value of horizontal integration.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: The Mukherjee Committee recommended:
options: Separation of malaria functions from family planning to allow each to be adequately staffed
questions.concept: This illustrates the recurring tension between vertical programmes achieving focus and horizontal integration achieving efficiency - a debate that continues in programme design.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health planning, committees & health policy
questions.stem: Health being a state subject in India means:
options: States have primary responsibility for delivering health services, with the centre setting policy and providing funds
questions.concept: This constitutional division explains wide inter-state variation in health outcomes and the use of centrally sponsored schemes with conditional funding to drive national priorities.
